title: Gluttony, Sexual Immorality and Love of Money with Their Opposites
english: Gluttony is the mother of sexual immorality. It feeds anxious thoughts and leaves fasting feeble. It muzzles ascetic practice and scares disciplined reflection away. It pictures dishes vividly and traces seasonings in shadow. It is a colt let loose and a madness without a bridle. It is a vessel of sickness and the envy of health. It blocks the passages, makes the bowels groan, and brings insult to its limit. It is the close companion of sexual immorality, the filth of the mind, and the sickness of the body. It brings burdensome sleep and a joyless death.

Self-control is the bridle of the stomach. It is the whip for insatiability, the standard for proportion, and the muzzle for voracious eating. It renounces ease and pledges itself to hard living. It tames thoughts and keeps its eye on wakefulness. It rescues from burning desire, trains the body, and stands as a tower in toils and a wall around conduct. It orders character and holds the passions back. It puts the limbs to death so souls may live again. It imitates the resurrection and lives the life of sanctification.

Sexual immorality is the offspring of greedy craving for food. It softens the heart and burns like a furnace. It leads idols to the bridal chamber and is an unnatural deed. It is a darkened face and an imagined embrace. It makes its bed in dreams and joins bodies without feeling. It cheats through the eyes and stares without shame. It brings shame into prayer and disgrace into the heart. It leads its followers into ignorance.

Chastity is the robe of truth. It is the axe laid to licentiousness, the charioteer of the eyes, and the overseer of thoughts. It cuts intention clean and cuts intemperance out. It grows against nature and stands against burning desire. It completes good works and labors alongside self-control. It is the lamp of the heart and the sure measure of prayer.

Love of money is the storehouse of idols. It prophesies to the crowd and is the reckoning of stinginess. It keeps strict account of deposits and grows rich into captivity. It breeds injustice and fattens diseases. It foretells long life, chants over love of labor, and counsels sleeplessness. It starves the stomach while praising cheap food. It is an insatiable madness and an evil full of many cares.

orientation: Evagrius now begins his paired list of vices and virtues with gluttony, sexual immorality and love of money.

title: Poverty, grief, joy, anger, patience
english: Poverty is the uprooting of love of money and the root of freedom from love of money. It is the fruit of love and a cross of life. It is a life without pain, a treasure free from envy, a heaven free from care, a sun that is never distracted, matter without measure, wealth beyond comprehension. It is a sickle for worry, a doing of the Gospels, a world that cannot be dissolved, a swift-footed athlete.

Grief lives with loss and keeps company with failure. It runs ahead of exile, remembers one's family, sits beside hardship, and travels with listlessness. It is an accusation of irritation, a reminder of insult, and a darkening of the soul. It is a downcastness of character, a drunkenness of prudence, a sleep-inducing antidote, a cloud over one's form, a worm of the flesh, a grief of thoughts, and a populace of captivity.

Joy is the destruction of grief and thanksgiving in misfortunes. It is a vision of prayers and gladness in labors, a cheerfulness in doing good, a planting of renunciation, a vessel of hospitality, a refuge of hopes, food for those in training, encouragement for those who mourn, comfort for tears, help in affliction. It is in agreement with love and of one mind with patience.

Anger is a plundering of prudence, an overturning of one's settled state, a confusion of nature, a wild appearance, a furnace of the heart, a belching flame, a law of fury, a wrath of insults, a mother of wild beasts, a silent battle, and a thorn in prayer.

Patience is a weapon of prudence, a courtroom for anger, and a place of healing for the heart, an admonition to the reckless, a calm for the troubled, a harbor without storms. It does good to those who cause grief, is gentle toward everyone, blesses when blasphemed, rejoices when insulted, is a comfort to the distressed, a mirror of the things hoped for, and a prize for those who suffer hardship.

orientation: Evagrius continues his catalogue of the eight principal vices and their opposing virtues, now giving the epithet-chains for poverty, grief, joy, anger, and patience.

title: Listlessness, endurance, vainglory, freedom from vainglory, envy, and the closing prayer
english: Listlessness is an airy friendship and a leading astray of footsteps. It hates hard work and battles stillness. It grows dizzy at psalm-singing and shrinks back from prayer. It slackens ascetic practice into untimely drowsiness and restless, turning sleep. It is a weight of madness and a hatred of the cell. It opposes labors and counterbalances perseverance. It muzzles meditation and leaves the Scriptures unlearned. It shares in grief and serves as a timepiece of hunger.

Endurance breaks off listlessness and cuts down thoughts. It keeps death in mind and meditates on the cross. It is fear nailed fast and gold under the hammer. It is a law book for afflictions and a book of thanksgiving. It is a breastplate for stillness and a weapon for labors. It is a fervent devotion to good work and a pattern for the virtues.

Vainglory is a fantasy of encounters and a pretense of hard work. It stands against the truth and leads the way for heresies. It hungers for the first seat and is last to offer a greeting. It is enslaved to praises, a spirit of many disguises, a beast with countless teeth. At its center vainglory is woven together with pride and envy, each living in the other and warring through the other. Together they are the chain of evils dragging in three ways, the draught of passions mixed with three poisons, and the threefold tongue of the heretics.

Freedom from vainglory is the working of humility. It breaks away from people-pleasing and pays no attention to praises. It contemplates knowledge and stands against the world. It gives the soul a keen sensitivity and teaches the doctrine of simplicity. It is a hiding place for labors and an enemy to reputation. It is a treasure hidden in a perishable body.

Envy is the clothing of pride and the stripping off of humility. It is the root of slander and a disease in the eye of cheerfulness. It counterfeits friendship and deceives with frankness. It hates love and burns against those who prove worthy. It unsettles those who stand firm and mocks those who are praised. It distorts the eyes. Who is pure in heart, who does not catch himself setting aside a commandment of God, or falling short, or in negligence? May our Christ prosper every work of his will. To him be glory forever. Amen.
